sections.h2: Who handles property tax in Sumner County?
sections.html:
The Assessor of Property, John M. Hurt, sets values from Room 206 of the building at 355 N. Belvedere Drive in Gallatin (615-452-2412, Monday to Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.). The office is on the second floor, just behind the Walmart. The Trustee, Cindy Williams, collects the tax from Room 107 in the same building (615-452-1260, same hours).

Address changes for tax bills also go through the assessor, because that office edits the roll from which the bills print. A new owner who wants the notice mailed to a different address should call 615-452-2412 after closing.

Property tax sales are not run by either office. The assessor's FAQ sends people to the Clerk and Master for tax sale information.

sections.h2: What makes Sumner County's housing market different?
sections.html:
Sumner County lies on Tennessee's northern border, about 25 miles northeast of Nashville, and belongs to the Nashville metropolitan area. It covers 543 square miles, with the Cumberland River long the main route for trade. Gallatin is the county seat and Hendersonville has the most people. Goodlettsville, Millersville, Mitchellville, Portland, Westmoreland and White House complete the eight cities, and several of them extend into neighboring counties.

Growth is the story here. The Census Bureau's QuickFacts show:

  • 215,538 residents in July 2025, up 9.8% from April 2020
  • 89,138 housing units, 72.0% owner-occupied
  • Median owner-occupied value of $393,100 for 2020 to 2024
  • Median gross rent of $1,424 and median household income of $90,301
  • 3,045 building permits in 2025, with 8.3% of residents in poverty

Schools are run by the Sumner County Board of Education, a twelve-member body with eleven elected district members and the Director of Schools. Because values here are higher than in Sullivan or Shelby, each point of tax rate matters more to a Sumner seller.

sections.h2: How is a Sumner County tax bill worked out?
sections.html:
The assessor lists four parts: appraised value, an assessment ratio set by state law, the assessed value, and the rate. Houses and farms are assessed at 25 percent of appraised value and commercial or industrial property at 40 percent. The county commission sets the county rate, and each city may add its own.

sections.h2: When and how do I pay Sumner County property tax?
sections.html:
Bills become due on the first Monday in October. Tax paid by February 28 carries no interest, and March 1 is the delinquency date. The Trustee accepts payment in these ways:

  • Online at tnpayments.com with Visa or Mastercard
  • By mail, with the top portion of the notice
  • In person at Room 107
  • By phone with a Visa or Mastercard
  • At local banks listed on the back of the notice

Card payments carry 2.65 percent plus $1, charged by the processor and not the Trustee. Up to five partial payments can be made by check or cash, and anything unpaid after February starts accruing interest on March 1. The paid status of a bill can be checked under the online payment link.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Sumner County valuation?
sections.html:
Call the assessor during the first week of May to book a hearing with the Sumner County Board of Equalization, which meets in June. An informal talk with the appraisal staff comes first and can be skipped. Compare your house with nearby sales and note any zoning or physical changes before you call.

The state's calendar sets May 20 as the date by which change notices should be mailed and exemptions applied for. A further appeal to the State Board of Equalization is due by August 1 or 45 days after the county board's notice, so for 2026 only owners with a later notice can still file. The assessor says values normally stay put between reappraisals, and the county is on a five-year cycle with the next one in 2029. Staff visit every property's exterior in between.

sections.h2: What relief and freeze programs does Sumner County run?
sections.html:
The Trustee runs the state tax relief rebate for elderly, disabled and disabled veteran owners, and a freeze for the county and some Sumner cities. Freeze applications for 2026 open in September 2026, relief applications are taken when bills go out, and the deadline is 35 days after the February payment date. Seniors 65 and over qualify on income. For disabled veterans and their widows, the programs are not income based. Everyone must requalify every year.

Appointments can be made by phone at 615-452-1260 or through the Trustee's online scheduler.

sections.h2: What does a house inside a Sumner County city pay?
sections.html:
An address inside a city limit owes the county rate plus the city rate. Using the posted figures on the same $200,000 house, a Gallatin address adds about $264.75 to the county's $711, for roughly $975.75. A Hendersonville address adds about $294.15, for roughly $1,005.15. These are illustrations of the arithmetic only, and cities may also levy special assessments, which the assessor says to ask each city about.

A rural address outside every city pays the county rate alone. That difference is worth checking on a listing, since two houses with the same appraised value can carry different bills.

sections.h2: Which other Sumner County deadlines can affect a seller?
sections.html:
The state calendar the assessor publishes lists dates that touch many owners:

  • January 1: the assessment date, when ownership and condition are fixed for the tax year
  • March 15: the deadline to apply for greenbelt
  • May 20: change notices are due out, and exemption applications are due
  • September 1: the cutoff for prorating tax on buildings moved, demolished, badly damaged or finished after January 1

Business owners get a personal property schedule by February 1 and return it by March 1. A seller who is also closing a business should ask the assessor whether the January 1 tangible property still shows on the roll.

sections.h2: What should a Sumner County seller do about the tax bill at closing?
sections.html: Ask the Trustee in Room 107 for the balance on the parcel and have the title company prorate it on the settlement statement. The assessment date is January 1, so the roll shows the owner from that date. A buyer who sees no bill should phone the Trustee and update the mailing address with the assessor.

faqs.q: What is the Sumner County property tax rate?
faqs.a: The assessor's page shows $1.421 per $100 of assessed value for the county. Gallatin adds $0.5295 and Hendersonville $0.5883 on its listing.

faqs.q: When is the next Sumner County reappraisal?
faqs.a: 2029. The assessor says the county is on a five-year reappraisal cycle.

faqs.q: Can I pay Sumner County property tax by card?
faqs.a: Yes. The Trustee takes Visa and Mastercard online or by phone. The fee is 2.65 percent plus $1 and goes to the processing company.

faqs.q: How do I appeal my Sumner County assessment?
faqs.a: Call the assessor at 615-452-2412 in the first week of May to schedule a hearing before the county board, which meets in June. Gather comparable sales first.

faqs.q: Does Sumner County have a tax freeze?
faqs.a: Yes. The Trustee administers a freeze for the county and part of its cities for owners 65 or older, and applications for 2026 began in September.
